{{Quote|Vuffi Raa and I are heading back to the Centrality because I've got a hunch I could make a quick fortune running cargo to those backward planets. And if that doesn't work, there are always the casinos in the Oseon system. It'll do me good to polish up my sabacc game. When you don't play, you get rusty.|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], to [[Roa]]|<ref name="The Hutt Gambit">''[[The Hutt Gambit]]''</ref>}}
The '''Centrality''', also known as the '''Tund sector''',<ref name="AGttSWU3">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> was a remote [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] consisting of several dozen [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], ruled by the [[Near-Human]] [[Centran]]s.       

==History==
===Early history===
The region was originally settled by [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] with a strong sense of freedom and frontier spirit who were fed up with the corruption of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]. The settlers embraced the harsh environment and saw their success as a victory of their hard work. Although they opposed strong, central governments, they eventually formed a loose [[Confederacy|coalition]] of trade and defense agreements known as the "Centrality" in [[3350 BBY]], giving birth to an insular civilization. The head of this league was called the "[[Scrivinir]]," which meant "head writer" in [[Old High Trammic/Legends|High Trammic]].<ref name="SWG5" /> During the last [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the Old Republic, the [[Factory world/Legends|industrial worlds]] were hit by economic depressions, while the [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworlds]] were hit by crop plagues. With the central government too weak and the more prosperous [[Planet/Legends|worlds]], like [[Oseon VII]], unwilling to help, the civilization of the Centrality crumbled back to poverty and its backwater reputation began.<ref name="SWG5" />

===Imperial era===
{{Quote|Wow, sounds like some of the stuff that happened to me in the Centrality. One bad guy after another. Get a fortune, lose a fortune. So&hellip; how's my ship?|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="Rebel Dawn">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref>}}
The Centrality sector was part of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], but due to its remoteness, maintained most of its independence and military strength. It was regarded as largely strategically unimportant by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], and he permitted [[Rokur Gepta]], a [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerer of Tund]] jurisdiction over the Centrality. The Imperial military placed a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] in the region, consisting mostly of older [[Starship/Legends|ships]].

The Centrality was classified as a [[Imperial client state]] and the Empire maintained an embassy in the Centrality.<ref name="Lords of the Expanse">''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''</ref>

The worlds in the Centrality, now supporting the Empire, had their industries revitalized.<ref name="SWG5" />

[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] had a series of adventures in this region of space with his [[Droid/Legends|droid]] ally, [[Vuffi Raa]], in the days when he was still owner of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].

===New Republic era===
After the [[Death/Legends|death]] of Palpatine, the Centrality maintained its independence but had little impact on [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] affairs. The people viewed the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] with skepticism but nonetheless signed a treaty of goodwill. The [[Centrality Navy]] was reinforced with old Imperial starships and proved to be a capable defense. However, with the Empire gone, the economy had once again started to collapse and [[Renatasian]] terrorism started to rise.<ref name="SWG5" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the Centrality was hit by a flood of [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] and the region became plagued by overpopulation, crime, and poverty, and work became extremely scarce. With the government in turmoil, [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]] [[Sris Lehhett]] initiated a bloody coup and installed himself as the new Scrivinir, while the former one, [[Ottdefa/Legends|Ottdefa]] [[Tavell Geen]] fled to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in exile. Lehhett halted immigration, started mass conscription and used [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] methods to keep the population in line. However, wealthier [[Star system/Legends|systems]], like [[Oseon system/Legends|Oseon]], loudly protested against his methods and threatened to secede.<ref name="SWG5" />

==Astrography==
{{Quote|The Oseon would also be happy to arrange sightseeing visits to Rafa Four, Trammis Three, the ThonBoka Star Cave Nebula, or other destinations in the Centrality.|[[Unidentified Oseon Resort manager]], to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]|<ref name="MF" />}}
Located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], the Centrality was bordered to [[Spinward]] by the [[Shadola sector/Legends|Shadola sector]], [[Trailing]] by the [[Calaron sector/Legends|Calaron sector]], Coreward by the [[Cadma sector/Legends|Cadma sector]], and rimward by [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

The Centrality was defined by two [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade routes]], the [[Cadma Conduit]] and the [[Falko Run]]. The Cadma Conduit connected the Centrality to the [[Triellus Trade Route/Legends|Triellus Trade Route]] at [[Junkfort Station/Legends|Junkfort Station]] via [[Dagelin Minor]]. The majority of the Centrality's planets were clustered Coreward on the Cadma Conduit, and included the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Erilnar]]; the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] world of [[Scillal]]; [[Lekua V]], famous for its universities; and the Oseon system, famous for its [[Flamewind of Oseon/Legends|Flamewind]] phenomenon. The Falko Run, running Rimward, included the factory world of [[Ringneldia II]], the agriworld of [[Dilonexa XXIII]], and the [[Quor'sav/Legends|Quor'sav]] homeworld of [[Uaua/Legends|Uaua]]. Farther out were [[Trammis III/Legends|Trammis III]], [[Paulking XIV]] and [[Douglas III]], infamous for their hostile wildlife. A third minor route, the [[Arleen Loop]], linked [[Arleen]] on the Falko Run to Lekua V via [[Rafa V]], the homeworld of the [[Pre-Republic era|pre-Republic]] [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]] species, renowned for its massive, ancient plastic [[pyramid]]s and [[Life-orchard|orchards]] of [[life-crystal]]s.<ref name="TEA" />

At the absolute rimward end of the Centrality, near the border with Wild Space, was the mysterious planet [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], home to the enigmatic [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-users]] known as the Sorcerers of Tund. To the [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] south, well beyond most travel routes, was the [[Open Sea/Legends|Open Sea]], an expanse largely devoid of [[Star/Legends|stars]] and planets. Ships that suffered [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] failure in the Open Sea were known to go undiscovered for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], and ancient wrecks that had been recovered were used as cautionary examples on [[Hosrel XI]], at the Open Sea's border. Also near the Open Sea was the [[Renatasia system/Legends|Renatasia system]], a lost colony of [[Grizmallt/Legends|Grizmallt]] settled in [[3950 BBY]]. The Open Sea was home to the [[Oswaft]], sentient space-borne creatures native to the [[ThonBoka]] [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Economy==
The Centrality economy was largely based on tourism and the export of vitality-boosting Rafan life-crystals and [[Zebitrope system/Legends|Zebitrope]] [[Lesai/Legends|lesai]]. Owing to its proximity to [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidics]] dominated the trade (the route to Zebitrope on the Cadma Conduit became nicknamed the "[[Kessel Hop]]"), and had significant influence over the [[Human/Legends|Human]]-dominated Centrality government on Erilnar.<ref name="TEA" />

Ringneldia II was the Centrality's main industrial center, though its products were produced according to a local measurement system that was totally incompatible with the galactic standard.<ref name="TEA" />
